reason: Harvested both strings by driving the master. The button is button.b-act[data-act=done], text "Done", 12px under the "What guests see" segment and 64px above "Delete this moment" (render-b.js:899). The sentence is p.b-behindNote, "2 done, the last of them 18 April. One thing is not going ahead." (render-b.js:332), owner branch only. The finding fails on four counts. (1) The 'undiluted for a screen reader' claim is factually wrong: the editor is h("div.b-edit#b-edit", { role: "group", tabindex: "-1", "aria-label": "Editing " + nameOf(record) }) (render-b.js:831-834), so the button is already inside a group whose accessible name states the job the finding wants stated. (2) The proposed aria-label makes it worse, not better: replacing the accessible name of a button whose visible label is "Done" with "Finished editing Send the invitations" drops the visible word from the accessible name entirely, which fails WCAG 2.5.3 Label in Name and stops speech input ("click Done") from reaching the editor's primary control - on an artifact whose audit gate is an AA gate. It also double-announces the group label. (3) The copy half rests on a false premise. The counted past moments in the fixture are demo-audience-item-yes and demo-audience-item-venue, both state "covered", whose own label in STATE_LABEL is "Complete" (fixture.js:70-80). The record does hold completion; "2 done" is not claiming more than the data, and the filter deliberately drops the cancelled one. Worse, "two done" is ratified language: DIRECTIONS.md:195 lists it under "What all three already refuse" - "All three say nine live, two done, one not going ahead" - as the direction's answer to the reference product's silently-dropped cancellation. The replacement is also weaker prose: "2 have happened" is a bare numeral on a present-perfect verb and breaks the parallel with the clause that follows it, "One thing is not going ahead." (4) The collision itself is over-read. At desk width - the owner's primary surface since round 9's fixed two-pane frame - the two strings sit in two independently scrolling panes 899px apart (measured at 1440x960 and 1280x900) and cannot be brought into one viewport at all; I scrolled the button to centre and the sentence stayed 1160px below the fold. Only in the single column at 390/768 are they co-visible, 387px and 526px apart, separated by a rule, the Delete action, the whole plan list and the "Behind you" heading. And the misreading has nowhere to land: there is no per-moment completion control anywhere in the editor or on a row, so "mark this moment done" is not an action the surface offers. "Done" as the dismissal of an editor is the most conventional word in shipped UI, used exactly this way by the named benchmarks. This is taste stated as a defect, attached to a fix that would introduce a real accessibility regression and overwrite ratified copy. Not a gate restatement - interaction-check.mjs:508-510 asserts by [data-act=done], never by name - but not a finding either.
